# shader_33 — 3x3 stride-1 convolution, 16 -> 16 channels

Source of truth: `asm/shader_33.spvasm`. One compute pass. It reads a 3x3
neighborhood from each of four sampled RGBA images (same resolution as the
output), applies a fixed (compiled-in) fp16 linear layer — a 3x3 convolution
with stride 1, 16 input channels (4 images x RGBA), 16 output channels —
followed by a per-channel affine remap, and stores the 16 output channels as
four RGBA8 storage images.

This is the same computation pattern as shader_32 with two differences:
four input images instead of two (36 taps instead of 18), and **no** x2
coordinate scaling (stride 1: output texel `p` maps to input texel `p`).
The weights and affine constants are entirely different (see appendix).
There is no UBO, no push constants, no spec constants, no shared memory,
no loops.

## 1. Interface

- Workgroup size: **16 x 16 x 1**.
- Built-ins used: `gl_GlobalInvocationID` (only `.xy`; `.z` is ignored).
- All descriptors are in **set 0**:

| binding | kind | format | access | role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | combined image sampler, 2D float | (sampled; format external) | read | input feature image 0 (taps 0-8; also the size used for UV normalization) |
| 33 | combined image sampler, 2D float | (sampled; format external) | read | input feature image 1 (taps 9-17) |
| 34 | combined image sampler, 2D float | (sampled; format external) | read | input feature image 2 (taps 18-26) |
| 35 | combined image sampler, 2D float | (sampled; format external) | read | input feature image 3 (taps 27-35) |
| 48 | storage image 2D | `rgba8` | write-only (`NonReadable`) | output channels 0-3; its size is also the bounds-check extent |
| 49 | storage image 2D | `rgba8` | write-only | output channels 4-7 |
| 50 | storage image 2D | `rgba8` | write-only | output channels 8-11 |
| 51 | storage image 2D | `rgba8` | write-only | output channels 12-15 |

## 2. Behavior

Notation:

```
p       = ivec2(gl_GlobalInvocationID.xy)          // output texel
outSize = imageSize(out48)                          // binding 48 only
inSize  = vec2(textureSize(in32, 0))                // binding 32 only
uv      = (vec2(p) + 0.5) / inSize                  // texel center of p — stride 1
```

Early-out: if `p.x >= outSize.x || p.y >= outSize.y` (signed compare against
binding 48's size) the invocation returns without writing anything. The
unsigned gid is bitcast to signed first; there is no lower-bound check.

All four input images are sampled at the same `uv`, normalized by binding
32's level-0 size (the shader assumes the four inputs share that size — a
different-sized input would be sampled at scaled coordinates).

### 2.1 Taps

36 taps, each a `vec4` sampled with explicit LOD 0 and then converted to
fp16 (`f16vec4`). With `D = [(-1,-1), (-1,0), (-1,1), (0,-1), (0,0), (0,1),
(1,-1), (1,0), (1,1)]`:

```
t[0  + k] for k = 0..8 :  textureLodOffset(in32, uv, 0.0, D[k])
t[9  + k] for k = 0..8 :  textureLodOffset(in33, uv, 0.0, D[k])
t[18 + k] for k = 0..8 :  textureLodOffset(in34, uv, 0.0, D[k])
t[27 + k] for k = 0..8 :  textureLodOffset(in35, uv, 0.0, D[k])
```

(the (0,0) taps use no offset instruction operand; the others are
compile-time constant offsets, i.e. `textureLodOffset`).

### 2.2 Per output image

For each output image `o` in {48, 49, 50, 51} there are 36 constant `f16mat4`
matrices `W[o][k]` (one per tap) and three constant `f16vec4`s `a[o]`, `b[o]`,
`c[o]`. The value written at `p` is:

```
sum   = W[o][0]*t[0] + W[o][1]*t[1] + ... + W[o][35]*t[35]     // f16vec4
v     = (sum - a[o]) * b[o] + c[o]                             // componentwise, fp16
imageStore(out_o, p, vec4(v))                                   // rgba8 unorm store
```

- `(W*t)[i] = sum_j W[i][j]*t[j]`, `W[i][j]` row-major per the appendix.
- All arithmetic is IEEE fp16. The 35 additions associate strictly
  left-to-right in ascending tap order k = 0..35:
  `((W0*t0 + W1*t1) + W2*t2) + ...`. (In the original binary the terms are
  merely scheduled interleaved with sampling; the association order of each
  output's chain is exactly ascending tap order.) Reproduce this order for
  bit-exactness.
- The `rgba8` store clamps each component to [0,1] and quantizes to unorm8;
  this clamp is the only nonlinearity in the pass.

All four outputs are written at the same `p` from the same 36 taps; they
differ only in weights and affine constants.

Interpretation (hint, not normative): a stride-1 3x3 conv layer of a small
convolutional network operating on a 16-channel feature tensor packed as
4 RGBA8 images (e.g. the output of shader_32); `(x-a)*b+c` maps activations
into [0,1] for quantized RGBA8 storage.

## 3. Control flow

- Single early-out bounds check (section 2), guarding everything.
- No loops, no other conditionals; straight-line code otherwise.

## 4. Boundary behavior

- Writes are guarded only by the check against binding 48's `imageSize`; the
  other three outputs are assumed to be at least as large.
- Nothing clamps the sample UVs; border taps (texel -1 or `inSize`) resolve
  via the externally supplied sampler's address mode.
- The dispatch is expected to cover `outSize` (ceil(outSize/16) workgroups
  per axis); overhanging invocations self-terminate.

## 5. Precision requirements

Identical to shader_32:

- fp32 sample results are converted to fp16 (round-to-nearest-even) before
  any arithmetic.
- All matrix/add/affine math in IEEE fp16
  (`GL_EXT_shader_explicit_arithmetic_types_float16`).
- Accumulation association order of section 2.2.
- Widen to fp32 only for the final `imageStore`.

In GLSL, build each `f16mat4` from the row-major appendix tables as
`f16mat4(col0, col1, col2, col3)` with `col_j = f16vec4(W[0][j], W[1][j],
W[2][j], W[3][j])`, then use plain `M * t`.

## 6. Weights appendix

Layout: for each output binding, first the affine constants `a`, `b`, `c`
(as used in `v = (sum - a)*b + c`), then the 36 matrices keyed by
(input binding, tap offset), in tap order. Each matrix is printed as 4 rows
of 4 values, row-major; each value is exact decimal followed by the exact
fp16 hex-float in parentheses. All values are exactly representable in fp16;
both forms are bit-exact.
